QF.id: VI Functions of DP Account Opening_29

question.text: Partnership firm demat accounts should be opened in whose names?

answer.text: In the names of the partners, operated by the partners
In the name of the managing partner only
In the name of the firm with all partners as nominees

explanation.text: The Logic: A depository account cannot be opened in the name of a partnership firm because partnership firms cannot be members under the Companies Act. The account is therefore opened only in the names of the partners and is operated by the partners. The Trap: 'In the firm's name only' is not how partnership demat accounts work — they must be in the partners' names. Note: Partners provide the prescribed undertaking to comply with the Companies Act and other applicable statutes. The workbook also notes the maximum three-partner joint-account limit and the clearing-member account exception.
